problem_statement: Since the last deploy the abuse queue worker stops on the first closed report in a routine category. Closing a spam or harassment report through ManagedClient raises `KeyError: 'spam'` from the compliance check while the `report.closed` event is dispatched, so the reporter never gets a reply and the rest of the queue piles up. Reports in categories that do not need escalation should simply close. `python -m pytest -q tests` reproduces it (test_managed_client.py).

After the most recent deploy, the abuse queue worker halts as soon as it hits the first closed report in a routine category. When a spam or harassment report is closed via ManagedClient, the compliance check throws `KeyError: 'spam'` during dispatch of the `report.closed` event; as a result the reporter never receives a reply and the remainder of the queue backs up. Reports belonging to categories that don't require escalation should just close. You can reproduce this with `python -m pytest -q tests` (test_managed_client.py).

The abuse queue worker has been stopping on the first closed routine-category report ever since the last deploy. Closing a harassment or spam report through ManagedClient causes the compliance check to raise `KeyError: 'spam'` while the `report.closed` event is being dispatched. Consequently the reporter gets no reply and the rest of the queue accumulates. Expected behavior: reports in categories that need no escalation simply close. Repro: `python -m pytest -q tests` (test_managed_client.py).

Regression since the last deploy: on the first closed report in a routine category, the abuse queue worker stops. Using ManagedClient to close a spam or harassment report triggers `KeyError: 'spam'` from the compliance check during dispatch of the `report.closed` event, which means no reply ever reaches the reporter and the rest of the queue piles up behind it. Reports whose categories don't need escalation should close without anything further. Running `python -m pytest -q tests` reproduces the problem (test_managed_client.py).
